steps.note: Native whey is concentrated about 27-fold over a 10 kDa and then a 5 kDa membrane, kept cold.
This step is optional; at the whey's own pH of about 6.5 the purity is far lower.

steps.name: high pressure
steps.note: Held at 600 MPa, which makes beta-lactoglobulin aggregate and fall out while alpha-lactalbumin stays dissolved.
The clear supernatant is the alpha-lactalbumin fraction and the pellet holds the precipitated beta-lactoglobulin.

processing.text: These are the conditions of one pilot-scale study, which reached 46 % yield and 80 % purity of alpha-lactalbumin in the supernatant; commercial routes may differ.

links.name: Romo et al., Foods 2023: Separation of alpha-Lactalbumin Enriched Fraction from Bovine Native Whey Concentrate

sources.text: The steps, pressure, pH and yields are from this study, which separates the fraction from native whey concentrate.
